title: Mitigate model-flavor oscillation causing routing ripple & capacity starvation
creator: Sofia Patel
description: Summary: A production incident on 2026-02-17 caused sustained capacity starvation in EU region services, triggered by repeated cross-region reroutes and a model-flavor handshake mismatch. The routing system repeatedly offloaded traffic to a remote region and back, amplifying latency and exhausting reserved pools. This ticket tracks follow-ups, mitigations, and delivery plan to prevent recurrence.
timeline:
2026-02-17 09:03 UTC: Synthetic anomaly alert (latency + queue depth)
2026-02-17 09:07 UTC: Auto-fallback policies started rerouting traffic off EU to us-west-2
2026-02-17 09:11 UTC: Back-and-forth reroutes observed; EU dedicated pools hit 95% queued tokens
2026-02-17 09:26 UTC: On-call executed manual routing freeze and throttled cross-region failover
2026-02-17 10:12 UTC: Emergency rollback of an experimental policy rollout (policy-snapshot v2026-02-17-a)
2026-02-17 11:00 UTC: Incident declared, mitigation verified, postmortem investigation started
impact: ~4 hours of increased tail latency for customers routed through EU (observed p99 latency increased 3.2x), transient request errors (502/504) for <0.5% of requests, internal SLA burn for Dedicated customers in EU. Operationally, teams had to halt automated rollouts and drain pools, causing delayed deployments.
detection: Triggered by combined alerts: p99 latency + queue depth + model-serving error rate. SRE on-call correlation with routing telemetry (route-change rate spike) identified oscillation pattern within 8 minutes of anomaly detection.
root_cause: A chain of faults: (1) a recently merged routing policy changed model-flavor mapping semantics to favor 'flavor affinity' weights without updating the handshake checksum logic, (2) a stale policy snapshot propagation bug allowed a mismatch between control-plane policy and data-plane flavor tags, (3) affinity TTL was configured too short (30s) which enabled aggressive re-affinity decisions, and (4) the circuit-breaker that should have rate-limited cross-region adoption used a static threshold that failed to account for rapid bidirectional churn. The net effect: repeated cross-region reroutes and rehydration of remote KV caches, which amplified load and caused capacity starvation.
mitigation_taken: Fast mitigations during incident: 1) froze policy rollouts globally, 2) disabled the experimental affinity-weight policy flag, 3) applied a temporary increased affinity TTL to 10 minutes, 4) manually enforced a 60s cooldown for cross-region failovers, and 5) drained and reprovisioned EU reserved pools to restore headroom.
long_term_solution_summary: Introduce a handshake checksum for model-flavor mapping, implement adaptive circuit-breaker with backoff tied to route-change velocity, add policy snapshot validation in the control plane, extend default affinity TTLs and add safety caps to automated re-affinity, and expand routing simulation tests in staging to include synthetic oscillation scenarios.
action_items: A1: Implement handshake-checksum for flavor tags (control-plane + runtime) and add mismatch alarm - owner: @liam - estimate: 5
A2: Replace static circuit-breaker with adaptive algorithm that throttles based on recent route-change velocity and capacity headroom - owner: @tanya - estimate: 8
A3: Increase default flavor-affinity TTL from 30s -> 10m and make TTL tunable per-policy with lower bound safeguards - owner: @evan - estimate: 3
A4: Add control-plane snapshot validator that rejects rollouts where data-plane flavor tags disagree with intended mapping; add canary gates - owner: @liam - estimate: 3
A5: Create synthetic chaos tests that simulate flavor-handshake failures and cross-region oscillation, run on each pre-release for routing-service - owner: @test-eng - estimate: 5
A6: Dashboard: new panel for route-change velocity, flavor-tag mismatch rate, cross-region failover counts, and adaptive-circuit-breaker trips - owner: @nora - estimate: 2
A7: Update runbooks and on-call playbook with steps to detect and freeze policy rollouts and recommended throttles - owner: @sre - estimate: 1
A8: Post-implementation canary in EU for 72h, followed by staged global rollout with metric gates - owner: @product - estimate: 2
progress_updates: 2026-02-20: Investigations complete; agreed on handshake-checksum design and adaptive breaker approach in architecture sync.
2026-02-25: Prototype circuit-breaker merged to internal feature branch; initial synthetic tests passing but need production-mirroring load tests.
2026-03-04: Control-plane snapshot validator implemented; added preflight check rejecting mismatched rollouts in staging.
2026-03-10: TTL change rolled to canary in eu-west-1; no regressions after 48h; scheduling full EU rollout next week.
2026-03-13: Documentation and runbook PR created; awaiting SRE review and sign-off.
postmortem_summary: The incident was not caused by a single binary bug but by an interaction between a policy semantics change and insufficient safety controls in routing orchestration. Our mitigations and planned work address both surface-level symptoms (TTL, throttles) and deeper systemic issues (control-plane/data-plane consistency, adaptive failure suppression). Expected reduction in recurrence risk after A1-A4; will monitor via new dashboards and automated alerts.
acceptance_criteria: Handshake-checksum deployed to runtime and control-plane; no flavor-tag mismatch alerts in 7 days of canary traffic.
Adaptive circuit-breaker reduces route-change velocity under synthetic oscillation in staging by >= 90% without increasing p99 latency more than 10%.
Policy snapshot validator blocks mismatched rollout attempts in pre-release and provides clear failure reason to operator.
New dashboards show stable route-change velocity < baseline under at least two high-traffic spikes during canary period.
